why: VERDICT.md quotes the number of findings the two pre-freeze reviews of preregistration 0011 raised; a number quoted in prose must trace to an artifact, and until 2026-09-03 this one traced only to commit messages.

rounds.note: five lenses (shield, prereg-reader consistency, script, mutation coverage, record), two refuters per finding; the subagent quota expired during refutation, so 15 findings were adjudicated by hand against the code; many rejections are refuters reading files already fixed mid-review
confirmed_titles: Disjointness clause is satisfied by CLI echoes, not by the data; the cache-reuse path can bank the 1024 corpus as a 2048 corpus at offset 75000
Prereg says the slope clause uses a cluster bootstrap 'as corrected 2026-08-31'; the script banks the fragment-level (anti-conservative) interval and no cluster bootstrap code exists in the repo
The transfer arm — the one arm the gutenberg pool leak actually crosses — has no gutenberg-excluded clause, though the script banks the number
NaN / Infinity values pass every numeric clause and yield CARVE_ROBUST
Preregistered run parameters (seed, rungs, matched rung, chunk count) are neither banked nor enforced; the transfer model can be given 8x the data and a seed sweep would be invisible
rejected_titles: The reader states a boundary bracket for runs the data does not support: scope failures and NOT-RUN-shaped artifacts are bracketed as measured failures, and a void transfer arm is bracketed as SIZE_SPECIFIC
within_split_is_grouped_by_source is a hard-coded constant, so the split clause can never fail on a script-produced artifact
run_carve.py defaults point at the banked 0007 artifacts and label; a 0011 run must override five flags and the reader does not check the preregistration label
The id 0011 is already promised in the strategy documents to a different preregistration (M1 per-head recipe search)
within_slope clause names a cluster bootstrap that no code performs; the reader will gate on a fragment-level interval
scope_carve and disjointness clauses gate on CLI echoes; a reused 1024 cache would pass as a 2048 corpus at offset 75000
A wrong-size or short-ladder artifact is not rejected: the reader emits CARVE_FAILS with boundary (2048, 4096] and exit 0
The transfer clause's 'trained on corpus A at 100000' is not checked; matched_rung is a free CLI argument the reader only echoes
disjointness bar entry declares lower_is_better for a >= 75000 condition; scope_carve declares higher_is_better for an equality
Seed is sealed in the prereg scope but the measurement artifact never banks it
Scope says the transfer arm is 'compared at' the 100000 rung, but every bar clause compares it against a baseline trained on the 500000-row top rung
A void transfer arm (shared chunks or bad offset) is reported as a transfer that 'does not' pass, yielding a substantive CARVE_SIZE_SPECIFIC verdict
Script banks the fragment-level (anti-conservative) slope interval into the field the 0011 slope clause judges; the prereg's claim that scaling.py was 'corrected' to a cluster bootstrap is false
Registered claim quotes the superseded lower bound and its `reverify` is the default run_carve.py invocation, which would overwrite the audit-corrected 0007 artifact
`corpus_b_chunk_offset` and `carve_bytes` are argument echoes, not data-derived; the cache-reuse path performs no consistency check
Artifact does not record how many rows the baselines were trained on, so the 'same rows as the top rung' clause is unverifiable from the banked file
Reader files a CARVE_FAILS verdict with a 2048 boundary for a wrong-size artifact instead of rejecting it as the prereg says
No OOM or disk defect (estimate, no action): peak RSS about 7.3 GB of 16.5 GB; corpus C cache about 2.89 GB of 5.2 GB free
Bar text promises a cluster bootstrap that the pipeline does not run; within_slope clause will be evaluated on the fragment-level interval
Scope and disjointness clauses are checked against CLI-argument echoes; the default --cache reuses the 1024 corpus and stamps it carve_bytes=2048 / offset 75000, which the reader accepts
matched_rung has no clause: a transfer model trained on corpus A's 800000 rung passes as CARVE_ROBUST
The reference_carve_bytes scope clause has no mutation case
The frozen-set within-margin mutation is not isolating: its fixture also fails the transfer-margin clause
Transfer arm — the arm the disjointness clause guards — has no gutenberg-excluded clause although the script banks transfer_top1_non_gutenberg
within_split_is_grouped_by_source and corpora_share_source_chunks can never be false in a script-produced artifact; the control fixture passes on literals
Several reader branches have no mutation, and the generic missing-field case fires two clauses at once
Reader does not check the preregistration stamp, and run_carve.py's defaults for --preregistration/--out/--scores-out are 0007's banked paths
The within_slope clause claims a cluster bootstrap that no code in the repository performs; the field the reader reads will be the fragment-level interval the audit called defective
The thesis's failure mechanism repeats the prior the record explicitly recorded as wrong: the alignment features carry about one accuracy point and are not the casualty
why_now states this run's cost as the 1024 run's banked cost, dropping the EXTRAPOLATION label MILESTONES.md attaches to the same projection
why_now_despite_the_milestone_sequencing is a rationalisation in its argument, honest only in what it admits
The 'boundary to a factor of two' framing compares a 2048 result at a 500000-fragment top rung against a 4096 pass measured at 800000, and assumes a single monotone crossing
The transfer arm can emit CARVE_ROBUST on rows the prereg itself says the disjointness guarantee does not cover; the covering number is banked and never read

run_carve.py reuses any existing --cache without checking carve or offset, and writes carve_bytes and corpus_b_chunk_offset from the command line rather than from the data; defaults still point at 0007's corpus and banked artifacts
'Makes the bar stricter than 0007's' invites the wrong reading: on the record the gutenberg-excluded margin is expected to be the slackest of the three
The sealed field name corpus_b_chunk_offset refers to corpus C, while the prereg defines Corpus B as the 1024 corpus whose banked offset is 50000
Reader docstring calls this run 'the M3 carve-size arm' while the prereg says it is not M3's; both get sealed together
The title asserts unqualified disjointness from both earlier corpora, the sentence class the audit found false for the gutenberg family

rounds.note: four lenses over the revised files; only the shield and statistics lenses completed before the quota expired and no refuter ran; all 17 findings were adjudicated by hand against the code, 16 acted on, 1 (no OOM/disk defect) recorded as not a defect
rejected_titles: Reference corpus identity is a command-line echo; the reader gates the echo and ignores the measured chunk-id range that would expose a swap
Corpus C's chunk offset is sealed only as a lower bound, so the sealed corpus can be redrawn at any higher offset and re-read until it passes
The evaluation fraction and source chunk size are neither banked nor gated, and each changes every measured number while leaving every sealed count exactly right
carve_bytes == 2048 cannot fail on a legacy cache: the prereg says the value comes from build metadata, but the reader does not check carve_bytes_source
The transfer model's accuracy on its own corpus is never measured, so a SIZE_SPECIFIC verdict cannot distinguish a transfer failure from a retraining failure
Under CARVE_FAILS the emitted boundary (2048, 4096] asserts that 4096 clears the 0007 protocol's bar at a 500000-row top rung, which has never been measured
Banked margins are rounded to 4 dp before the reader subtracts them in binary float, so a margin the artifact prints as 0.0500 can read as either pass or fail
The artifact banks nothing that identifies the gutenberg pool corpus C was built from, and the corpus manifest cannot cover a 2048 cache
The script's default --out and --scores-out are 0007's banked artifacts and no 0011 invocation is documented anywhere in the repository
Frozen reader cannot tell a cluster-level slope bound from a fragment-level one; the prereg's stop rule is unenforced
Banked cluster intervals reproduce only at 4000 resamples; the script hardcodes 2000 and no file records 4000 for 0006/0007
scaling.py CLI ignores the eval_chunk_ids the score files carry and emits the anti-conservative fragment interval
The cluster-bootstrap branch that 0011's slope gate depends on has no test in the mutation gate
Prereg 0011 dates the fitter's cluster correction to 2026-08-31; it landed 2026-09-02
scaling.py DEFECT note claims every interval was understated by ~45%; the 0007 interval 0011 inherits widened by 6%
audit_rederivations.json banks a null upper bound for 0007's superseded fragment-level interval
Only run_carve.py banks a cluster interval; run_study.py and run_topk.py still fit without groups, and the post-audit seed re-runs bank unlabelled fragment-level intervals
